title: Rollout Chronograph — Pocket Guide & Staggered Cadence Notes (Feb 2026 draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact operational playbook and staggered-cadence planner for medium-impact releases where we need predictable latency and minimal blast radius. Treat this as the quick pocket guide for the release owner and the on-call operator — not the full runbook.

Scope and when to use:
- Use for changes that touch serving routing, model variants, or traffic shaping.
- Intended for releases with multi-stage traffic shifts (micro-canary -> regional ramp -> global steady).
- Not for infra-wide kernel upgrades or datastore migrations (use the full migration runbook).

Quick decision grid (before sign-off):
- Feature flag toggles ready? (yes/no)  -> must be YES for staggered cadence.
- Smoke tests passing in staging for 24h?    -> recommend at least 1h for low-risk, 24h for medium.
- Observability hooks instrumented (latency histograms, error counters, token-cost metrics)? -> MUST have p50/p95/p99, request_count, trace sampling.
- Rollback button validated? -> practice off-ramp for canary (automated route-policy flip or model pin).

Preflight checklist (day -2 to day 0):
- [ ] Merge final release PR and note the SHA (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-procedures/pull/421).
- [ ] Attach release tag to deployment artifact and confirm artifact checksum.
- [ ] Run synthetic traffic run in staging (50–200 QPS) with representative prompt mix; collect p50/p99 and token-cost.
- [ ] Create a unique release channel in Sentry and Datadog; set temporary increased sampling for traces.
- [ ] Notify SRE and SLO owners in Slack channel #release-watch 24h prior.
- [ ] Prepare rollback play (document step-by-step toggle names & runbook snippets).

Staggered cadence calendar (example timeline, PST):
- Day 0, 09:00 — Release owner status call (15m): confirm go/no-go, note roll windows.
- Day 0, 10:00 — Micro-canary (1% global traffic, single region, subset of users) — 30m observation window.
- Day 0, 10:30 — If green, expand to 10% in region for 45m.
- Day 0, 11:30 — Regional ramp to 30% for 1h.
- Day 0, 13:00 — Cross-region validation, expand to 50% global (if metrics stable).
- Day 0, 15:00 — Global steady-state (100%) with continued elevated monitoring for 4h.
- Day 0+1, 09:00 — Post-deploy review and snapshotting (telemetry, sample prompts, user-facing checks).

Watchlist metrics (quick thresholds):
- Latency p50 increase > 20% from baseline -> investigate.
- Latency p99 increase > 30% or absolute > 800ms -> rollback candidate.
- Error rate increase > 0.5% absolute -> pause rollout and triage.
- Request success ratio < 99.2% or increased 5xxs in a 5-min sliding window -> abort and rollback.
- Token cost deviation > +15% -> evaluate model quantization/fallback policy.

Day-of runbook (concise operator steps):
1) Kickoff (09:00) — Confirm attendees: release owner, infra lead, SRE, in-region operator, product liaison.
2) Micro-canary (10:00) — Deploy variant A to canary pool; mark canary in console.
3) Observe (10:00-10:30) — Run smoke script (smoke-suite/canary-smoke.sh) and sample n=500 responses.
4) Triage -> If any watchlist metric triggers, call the abort channel and execute rollback plan:
   - Toggle feature off (feature_flag_name) -> routes revert to baseline model.
   - If flag fails, apply routing policy override: route-policy revert-2026-02.
5) Ramp steps as above. Record timestamps and telemetry snapshots for each step.

Communications templates (Slack snippets):
- Preflight ping (24h):
  "@channel Release 'chronograph-2026-02' scheduled for Tue 10:00 PST. Owner: @Evan. Micro-canary 1% -> regional ramp -> global. Will post play updates in this thread. JIRA: JIRA-1984"

- Abort ping (example):
  "@here ABORT: rolling back chronograph-2026-02 canary due to p99 latency breach > 800ms. Executing feature_flag toggle. See incident: https://sentry.redwood.ai/issue/xxxxx"

Release notes (draft) — high level for customer-facing changelog:
- New: Staggered routing support for hybrid model variants enabling lower tail latency for short-context requests.
- Improved: Default routing policy now prefers quantized v2 for low-cost bursts; fallback to full precision when confidence < 0.6.
- Fixed: Race condition in KV cache invalidation that could cause occasional stale prefix echoes under heavy burst.

Known issues to call out (internal):
- Observed a 3–5% spike in token-cost in staging under long-context load (PR mitigation planned).
- Region EU-west may have slightly higher cold-starts when autoscaler scale-in is tight (temporary throttle configured).

Post-deploy snapshot checklist (day 0+1):
- [ ] Capture telemetry snapshot: last-24h latency hist, error counters, cost-per-token.
- [ ] Collect 200 sample prompts and responses (random/stratified across UIDs) and run the quick QA script.
- [ ] Confirm SLO burn rate is within expected bounds.
- [ ] Close the release ticket with links to snapshots and runbook notes.

Quick templates and pragmatics
- Short rollback note (copyable):
  "Rolled back chronograph-2026-02 at 10:18 PST due to p99 latency increases. Reverted feature_flag: routing-chronograph and applied route-policy revert-2026-02. Refer to JIRA-1984 for postmortem."

Open questions / decisions pending:
- Do we require a mandatory 24h staging hold for all serving changes, or can we relax to 2–3h for low-risk model-only rollouts? (Ops proposal: 6h middle ground).
- Can SRE provide a quick auto-alert spec to trigger an automated traffic cut (e.g., circuit-break to 0.1%) if p99 > 1000ms for 2 consecutive windows?
- Finalize owner for release + backup owner rotation (need name for weekend releases).

Action items (owners):
- Evan: finalize rollback commands and confirm route-policy IDs (due: 2026-02-16).
- Lina: schedule increased trace sampling and provide trace links for day-of (due: 2026-02-17).
- Marcus: run longer synthetic run in staging with mixed prompts and post the telemetry snapshot (due: 2026-02-17).

Notes to self (hints / heuristics):
- Keep micro-canary windows short but non-zero — too short hides regressions, too long wastes ops time.
- Prefer staged regional ramps to spot infra-localized regressions (e.g., region-specific networking or image pulls).
- Log the exact artifact SHA in the release thread — searchability later saves hours.

Appendix: quick links
- Console: https://console.redwood.ai/releases/chronograph-2026-02
- SLO dashboard: https://datadog.redwood.ai/dash/slo/chronograph
- Incident channel: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/CRELEASES

(End of pocket guide)
